newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian politician says money was for property.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian politician says money was for property.

text.p: A Malaysian politician who was charged with trying to leave Australia with about A$1.2 million ($960,000) in cash said on Monday that the money was for a property purchase, the national Bernama news agency reported.
Selangor Chief Minister Muhammad Muhamad Taib told reporters in the state capital of Shah Alam that the money was entrusted to him by his brothers for a property purchase on Brisbane's Gold Coast.
Muhammad was detained at Brisbane airport on December 22 after the cash in Malaysian, Singaporean and New Zealand currencies was found in his luggage.
Under Australian law, people leaving the country must declare and justify taking out amounts worth more than A$5,000.
Muhammad told reporters on Monday he was not aware of the Australian law requiring him to declare the money.
"I did not realise that I had to declare the cash to be taken out of Australia," he said in his first public statement on the matter.
Muhammad said he had to bring back the money to Malaysia because two of his brothers could not be present for signing the purchase agreement.
"Therefore, we agreed that the money be taken back to Malaysia and we will settle the question of payment for the property within a one-month period," he said.
Meanwhile, Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Monday he had met with Muhammad about the incident, and urged the public and the press not to rush to conclusions.
"What I can say is that we should be fair in dealing with what he has said. We should not, out of prejudice, jump to conclusion," Mahathir told reporters at a function for national car maker Proton.
Asked whether Muhammad should be relieved of all his official duties until the matter was resolved, Mahathir said: "...Muhammad must be given a chance to explain."
"I've given some directive, some advice on what he should do," he added. He did not elaborate.
Asked whether Muhammad had mentioned an intention to resign, Mahathir said Muhammad had not stated his intentions.
The chief minister is vice-president of Mahathir's United Malays National Organisation (UMNO), the dominant political party in Malaysia.
News of Muhammad's arrest has prompted the country's opposition leader Lim Kit Siang to ask for a public declaration of his assets.
Muhammad was released unconditionally by Brisbane police after the arrest but has to reappear in the Australian city for a hearing on March 31.
